title: The check-in poster page has no iPhone path while the join pages do
what: When a member scans the desk check-in poster on an iPhone, the page only says the app is Android-only and to check in at the desk. The join page and the get-the-app page send iPhone users to the App Store once it is set, or explain the iPhone plan; the check-in page never reads the App Store link.
expected: All three member pages treat an iPhone the same way: once the App Store link exists, the check-in poster also offers it.
how_often: every iPhone scan of the check-in poster
fix_line: Give the check-in page the same iPhone and App Store handling as the join page

title: On an iPhone the gym invite link jumps to the App Store and the gym code is lost
what: The invite page promises iPhone users 'this same link will open it'. Once an App Store link is set, an iPhone is sent straight to the store before the gym's code is shown, and nothing carries the gym into the app after install, so the member arrives with no gym and no code.
expected: The member sees or keeps the gym's code (or the app opens the gym) after installing from the invite link.
how_often: every iPhone invite once the App Store link is live; cannot be proven in the cloud, needs a real-phone check
fix_line: Show the code first, or pass it through the store link, before sending an iPhone to the App Store

title: Choosing 'Pay at the desk instead' is never told to the gym
what: On the online join page, a new member who switches from paying online to paying at the desk only changes what their own browser tab remembers. The gym server is not told, so the gym's side can still show an online payment waiting for this person.
expected: Switching to desk payment is saved with the join request so the owner sees 'will pay at the desk'.
how_often: every time a member switches to desk payment after an online payment was started
fix_line: Send the desk-payment choice to the server and show it on the join request

title: Only test alerts report that they showed; real alerts leave no proof
what: When the admin app is closed, alerts arrive as browser pop-ups. Only a test alert tells the server it was shown on the device. A real alert (a member need) leaves no record, so the owner cannot tell whether yesterday's alerts ever reached his phone.
expected: Each real alert also records that it was shown (or why not), so the owner can see it reached his device.
fix_line: Report every shown alert, not only test alerts

title: The 'Become a member' card disappears silently when its check fails
what: The invite page asks the server whether the gym's online join works. If that call fails, the card simply stays hidden: nothing is logged and the owner never learns his online join was not offered.
expected: A failed check is at least logged so a broken online join can be found.
how_often: only when the server call fails

title: Freeze or extra days can run into a renewal already sold
what: Changing a future plan's start date checks the member's other plans for a clash, but adding freeze or gift days does not look at them at all. If the member already renewed, the old plan's new last day runs over the next plan's start, so the two overlap and the frozen days the member is owed are partly swallowed.
expected: Adding days either moves the following plan later too, or warns that it now overlaps the next plan.
who: members who renewed early and then freeze
how_often: every freeze on a member with a renewal already sold
fix_line: Check the member's later plans when adding days and shift or warn

title: Cancelling an online-paid receipt says nothing about the money already received
what: A receipt paid online through the gym's payment company saves itself. Cancelling it puts the full amount back on the member's dues, but the cancel sheet treats every receipt the same and never says the money is still with the gym and must be refunded at the payment company, so the member can be chased to pay again.
expected: For an online-paid receipt the cancel sheet says the money is still received and points to refunding it, or warns before re-opening the dues.
who: owners and members who paid online
fix_line: Show a refund note on the cancel sheet when the receipt was paid online

title: Date of birth is optional with no word that birthday wishes need it
what: The add-member form marks date of birth optional and gives no hint that birthday wishes and birthday counts depend on it. Mobile number has a hint saying why it matters; birthday does not, so the desk skips it and birthday features quietly reach fewer members.
expected: The birthday field says it is used for birthday wishes, and the owner can see how many members lack one.
how_often: every member added without a birthday; reach on Crispy Curves not counted (no database query in this step)
fix_line: Add a one-line hint under the birthday field

title: Phone-number sign-in appears only on the first-run welcome
what: 'Continue with your phone number' lives on the welcome screen, which shows only when the phone has no profile yet. A member who already set up the app never sees it. No other entry point was found in the code read for this step.
expected: Existing members can also find their gym by proving their number, for example from the Gym tab or Settings.
who: members who installed before the feature
fix_line: Offer the phone check outside the first-run welcome too

title: Waiting for the WhatsApp proof shows nothing when the check cannot reach the server
what: After the member sends the WhatsApp message, the app asks every few seconds whether it arrived. If that check gets no answer (no internet), the app silently tries again and keeps showing 'waiting', with no message that it cannot reach the server.
expected: After a failed check the screen says the internet seems off and to try again.
who: members signing in with their number
how_often: only on a weak or lost connection; cannot be proven in the cloud, needs a real-phone check
fix_line: Show an internet message when a status check fails

title: The gym page checks mobile numbers by a different rule than the other member pages
what: The bring-a-friend page uses the shared mobile-number rule that every copy must match (it reads digits typed in Hindi and other scripts). The gym page's question form has its own shorter rule, so the same number can be accepted on one page and refused on the other.
expected: The gym page uses the same shared mobile-number rule.
who: visitors typing in a non-English keyboard
fix_line: Use the shared mobile-number rule on the gym page
